why_realistic: The same shape as the classifier fallback that filed every unclassifiable item under tracks[0], which happened to carry the largest weight: a 'we have no information' branch is mapped to the most FAVORABLE value in reach instead of to unknown. Here a track with no posterior inherits the best posterior on the board, so an untried track is drawn as if it had already proven itself and the wide prior that makes it explorable is gone.
oracle:
"""A track with no history must cold-start at the configured prior, that is, at UNKNOWN.

Borrowing another arm's posterior fabricates evidence the new track never earned and destroys the
wide uncertainty Thompson sampling needs in order to explore it: every draw comes back near the
proven arm's mean, so the new track is either permanently favoured or never actually explored. The
assertions read the DRAWS, not the source."""
import bandit

CFG = {"scoring": {"bandit": {"prior_alpha": 1.0, "prior_beta": 1.0,
                              "explore_weight_lo": 0.5, "explore_weight_hi": 1.5}}}
PROVEN = {"proven": {"alpha": 60.0, "beta": 1.0, "n": 61}}


def test_an_unseen_track_draws_the_same_with_or_without_neighbours():
    with_peers = bandit.thompson_sample(PROVEN, ["fresh"], seed=3, cfg=CFG)["fresh"]
    alone = bandit.thompson_sample({}, ["fresh"], seed=3, cfg=CFG)["fresh"]
    assert with_peers == alone, (with_peers, alone)


def test_an_unseen_track_is_uncertain_not_confident():
    draws = [bandit.thompson_sample(PROVEN, ["fresh"], seed=s, cfg=CFG)["fresh"]
             for s in range(40)]
    assert min(draws) < 0.3, min(draws)
    assert max(draws) > 0.7, max(draws)


def test_the_cold_start_weight_is_not_pinned_to_the_top_of_the_band():
    ws = [bandit.explore_weight(PROVEN, "fresh", seed=s, cfg=CFG) for s in range(40)]
    assert min(ws) < 0.9, min(ws)
    assert 0.5 <= min(ws) and max(ws) <= 1.5, (min(ws), max(ws))
